subtype: Approach: simulates both success and things going wrong and prepares a response [Revision]
passage:
Seema: You used to say you just go on stage and it works. What changed?

Charu: A dead laptop, honestly. Two years ago mine died five minutes before a client talk and I stood there sweating. Now when I rehearse, I picture the good version, sure, but I also run two bad ones. One: the laptop dies. Two: someone asks, "Why is your number so different from last year?" For the first, I keep the slides on paper in my bag. For the second, I wrote a short answer on a card: what the number includes, and what I will check and send by evening. Last month the cable failed, I handed round the printouts, and nobody blinked.

Seema: And the tough question?

Charu: It came. The card was enough.

qa.q: What does Charu carry in case the laptop dies?
qa.a: Charu keeps the slides on paper in the bag.

qa.q: How did Charu feel when the laptop died two years ago?
qa.a: Charu felt panicked and anxious, standing there sweating five minutes before the client talk.

qa.q: What else could Charu prepare for?
qa.a: Charu could prepare for losing the slides file by keeping a copy on a memory stick or emailed to the host.

qa.q: How might the audience have seen the printouts when the cable failed?
qa.a: The audience might have seen Charu as calm and well prepared, since nobody blinked and the talk carried on.

grounding: Shows a presenter adding rehearsals of a dead laptop and a hard question, then carrying printouts and a prepared answer.
